You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Copper Clad Laminate Price Hike Enters Profit Validation Phase: Taiwan Union Technology and Elite Material Surpass Q2 Expectations Alongside Trainium 3 Ramp-Up

TEXT:
TL;DR
1. Taiguang Electronics reported revenue of NT$47.275 billion in Q2 2026, a quarter-on-quarter increase of 43%, with gross margin rising to 33.9% and net profit at NT$9.873 billion; Taimiao reported revenue of NT$14.301 billion, a quarter-on-quarter increase of 42%, with gross margin at 29.7% and net profit of NT$2.342 billion. Both Taiguang Electronics and Taimiao have demonstrated that price increases, product mix upgrades, and improved capacity utilization are translating into profits, though Taiguang Electronics' outperformance is more pronounced.
2. The third quarter is the next hurdle. Citi expects the shortage of high-end copper-clad laminates to continue from Q3 2026 through 2027, and Taiguang Electronics does not rule out a further price hike; if Taimiao follows suit and successfully ramps up its Thai production (starting July, UTC+8) and meets demand from Amazon Trainium 3, its profit margin could continue to rise.
3. The fundamental difference between Taiguang Electronics and Taimiao is already reflected in earnings revisions. Citi raised its earnings forecasts for Taiguang Electronics by 37%, 20%, and 16% for 2026, 2027, and 2028, respectively, raising the target price from NT$5,100 to NT$6,000; Taimiao's earnings forecasts for the same periods were only raised by 3%, 1%, and 1%, with the target price maintained at NT$1,950. The former's profit baseline is being rewritten, while the latter's growth logic is simply being confirmed.
4. The target prices appear attractive, but are based on aggressive profit projections for 2027 and valuation at cyclical highs. Taiguang Electronics' target price is based on 30x 2027E EPS, Taimiao’s on 25x; both near their respective historical highs. If M9, AI ASIC, 800G, and Trainium 3 deliver, earnings can support valuation; if share, yield or materials supply falters, both multiples and profits will correct downward.
5. The final sanity check is cash flow. Citi estimates free cash flow for Taiguang Electronics and Taimiao at negative NT$17.848 billion and negative NT$12.342 billion in 2026, only turning positive in 2027. Currently, this can be interpreted as expansion and stocking up for growth, but if receivables, inventories and capex continue consuming profits, the so-called “high-end materials platform” might still be valued by the market as a cyclical manufacturer.
Contents
I. What this Citi report truly adds
II. Q2 Outperformance: Price, Product Mix, and Utilization All At Play
III. Why a Further Price Hike Is Possible in Q3
IV. Taiguang Electronics: Profit Baseline Rewritten, M9 Is Next
V. Taimiao: Validation from Trainium 3, Thai Capacity Determines Slope
VI. How to Choose Between the Two Companies: Platform vs. Project
VII. Remaining Chapters
The narrative for high-end copper-clad laminates is shifting from “strong demand, tight supply” to a financial reporting verification phase—can price hikes convert to profit, and can capacity expansion result in cash flow? Taiguang Electronics and Taimiao’s Q2 report cards offer the first high scores, but Citi’s modeling for growth assumptions in 2027 has also raised subsequent hurdles considerably.
I. What this Citi report truly adds
Over the past few months, the industry logic for high-end copper-clad laminate has been well-established: AI GPU, cloud vendors’ proprietary ASICs, and the upgrade to 800G/1.6T switches are increasing board layer counts and signal speeds, thus upping the value of low-loss laminates, high-end copper foil, glass fiber cloth, and resin. Previously, discussions such as “Re-rating of Board Interconnects in the Age of AI” focused on denominators, with “Share and Effective Capacity Updates at Shengyi Technology” targeting market share and usable capacity. Today’s report offers new evidence: Taiguang Electronics and Taimiao have already written denominator growth into their Q2 profit statements.
This isn’t a case of “better-than-expected earnings” as a simple summary. Taiguang Electronics’ Q2 revenue was 21% above Citi’s forecast, but net profit was up by 41%; Taimiao’s revenue was in-line, but operating profit beat by 2%. The former demonstrates increases in revenue, price, and product mix; the latter shows that even without revenue surprises, margin can improve thanks to hikes and utilization. In other words, earnings drivers for high-end copper-clad laminate are shifting from just volume growth to a triple lever: volume, ASP, and product structure.
